# Model card: Invoice extraction

| | |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Read invoice header fields and line items, each with a verbatim quote. |
| Workflow | pay |
| Code | `pairly_pay.invoice_graph.read_with_model` (engine: `pairly_core.extraction.engine.extract`, schema `pairly_pay.invoice_schema.PayInvoice`) |
| Prompt | `core_extract` version `v1`, file SHA-256 `af089775e5e1419c...` |
| Output schema | `ExtractionOutput` |
| Model tiers, cheapest first | `small` (anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, openai `gpt-6-luna`) then `large` (anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5`, openai `gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Temperature | 0.0 |
| Output token limit | 8192 |
| Confidence threshold to accept | none |

## Inputs

The sanitised invoice text as a delimited data block, the schema description, and the organisation's own corrections as hints.

## Outputs

Per field and line: a value, a quote and a confidence, checked in code like every extraction. E-invoices (UBL, CII, Factur-X) are read from their XML without the model.

## Human oversight

Low-confidence or flagged values send the invoice to the exceptions queue. The validation and fraud checks run on the values, and a person approves every invoice (`approve`, second factor).

## Limits

* Scans depend on OCR quality.
* The offline Pay eval uses the ground truth as the read values, so it measures the checks, not extraction.
* Every call is logged in `model_calls` (prompt version and hash, model, inputs, output, tokens, cost) and fails closed: no model means a person does the step.
